instruction: Play the streaming video located at: https://demo.unified-streaming.com/k8s/features/stable/video/tears-of-steel/tears-of-steel.ism/.m3u8
source: Unified Streaming demo content - Tears of Steel HLS stream

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task variation using Unified Streaming Tears of Steel demo. Uses existing is_vlc_playing metric with URL validation. Similar complexity to original.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: (1) VLC is playing, and (2) the correct URL is being played
Parameter handling is correct: metric function receives rule dict directly without the 'expected.get(rules)' anti-pattern
Getter logic is sound: fetches VLC status.xml via HTTP interface which contains playing state and URL information
URL matching logic has multiple fallback methods (direct match, filename match for HLS streams, domain/path comparison) which is appropriate for streaming URLs
Complete instruction coverage: instruction requires playing a specific streaming URL, evaluator checks both playing state and URL match
Edge cases handled: returns 0 when not playing, handles missing URL info with warnings
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: For HLS streams (.m3u8), VLC's XML representation may vary across versions. The current multiple fallback approach is good, but runtime testing should verify that at least one of the XML paths contains the URL information for this specific stream
